story.title: Every viral clip has a
story.description: This is the journey of one small moment, from lost inside a long video to watched by thousands.

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: A golden moment, buried
chapters.text: Raka just wrapped a two-hour podcast. At minute 47 there was one answer that had everyone laughing, but nobody got around to cutting it. The moment quietly sank among thousands of other seconds.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: A clipper finds it
chapters.text: Nadia, a clipper, opens the source from Collaclips. She watches, takes notes, then stops at one point: "There it is." Her eyes are trained to find the 30 seconds worth watching.

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: Cut and polished
chapters.text: Nadia trims it to 34 seconds, adds captions, and puts the funniest part in the first three seconds. Viewers decide to stay or swipe in a heartbeat, so the opening has to hook right away.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: Approved together
chapters.text: The clip goes to Raka. He watches it, leaves a small note, then approves it. The creator stays in control and the clipper's work is respected. A clean collaboration for both sides.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: It spreads everywhere
chapters.text: The clip goes live on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. People who had never heard of Raka are now watching, laughing, and searching for the full video.

story.closing: One small moment, a big reach. That's what we help make happen, for creators and clippers.

faq.title: Frequently asked
faq.description: Can't find your answer? Reach out through the contact options below.

items.a: Collaclips is a platform that connects creators with clippers. Creators share source material, and clippers cut it into short clips for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.
Pick your role, creator or clipper, then contact us using the options below. We'll help you from the very first step.

items.q: What kind of material can be clipped?
items.a: Long videos such as podcasts, live streams, tutorials, and educational content that creators share through Collaclips.
Not necessarily. What matters is that you can spot interesting moments and know the basics of video editing. You can start with short source material and grow from there.

items.q: Do creators lose control of their content?
items.a: No. Creators choose which material to share and approve every clip before it goes live.

items.q: How do creators make sure the clips turn out right?
items.a: Every clip is sent to the creator for review. A clip only goes live once the creator approves it.
Clips are made in a vertical format that suits TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.
The collaboration terms and revenue split are agreed on together before a project starts. Contact us for the full details.
